newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends firmer, May-July widens.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends firmer, May-July widens.

text.p: CSCE world sugar prices ended mainly firmer on Thursday, with the gains concentrated in the spot May contract.

Traders said persistent buying of the nearby May-July switch underpinned prices throughout the session, driving the market up to just beneath the previous day's highs. But trade selling prevented the market from making further upside progress, they said.
"You had some late short-covering in the may-july spread, and some local buying," said one trader. "But there was good selling at every point up."
May sugar rose 0.07 cent a lb on the day, to 10.93 cents, after trading from 10.82 to 10.94. July futures gained 0.01 cent, to 10.68, while the outer months finished up 0.04 to down 0.03.

Some light fund buying was noted just ahead of today's close, which may give the market impetus to test the 11.00 cent barrier on Friday. But any upswing would run into good selling by producers and the commercial sector, traders said.
"We could move a bit higher, but it's not going to last," the trader said, noting heavy resistance at 11.15-11.19 cents (basis May.) Major support was seen at 10.75, followed by 10.68.
An estimated 10,332 lots were exchanged on the day, compared with an official total of 14,314 for March 4.
((-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1640))
